# orders-api policy pack (Pulumi CrossGuard, cloudrun)

Generated by `docuconf pulumi policy -target cloudrun` from the `orders-api` contract. It applies the rules `docuconf lint pulumi` applies to a preview ([spec/IAC.md](https://github.com/Docuconf/docuconf-go/blob/main/spec/IAC.md) sections 6.3 and 7.2) during `pulumi preview` and `pulumi up`, to every stack that uses a `orders-api` component generated from the same contract:

- each workload whose app container takes a component's env sets no undeclared name (`undeclared_input`), no name twice (`duplicate_env`), no secret as a plain value (`secret_as_value`), and every name the component renders (`unbound_container`);
- a value written into the container by hand passes the contract's checks, as the app would run them at boot (`invalid_value`);
- file inputs are mounted where the app reads them, whole and read-only (`mount_mismatch`), the pod metadata an injector asks for is on the pod template (`pod_metadata_missing`), and `envFrom` is refused (`env_from_unchecked`);
- a component generated from another version of the contract fails (`stale_module`).

`docuconf-orders-api` is mandatory: its findings fail the update. `docuconf-orders-api-advisory` reports a component no workload takes (`module_unused`).

A workload whose containers are unknown at preview is not checked; the component checks the values when they resolve.

## Use

```sh
npm install
pulumi preview --policy-pack path/to/this/directory
```

Or publish it (`pulumi policy publish`) and enforce it from Pulumi Cloud. Settings, in a `--policy-pack-config` file:

```json
{ "docuconf-orders-api": { "unmanagedEnv": ["OTEL_SERVICE_NAME"], "allowEnvFrom": false } }
```

Regenerate it rather than edit it when the contract changes.
